name: CreateOS Sandbox (NodeOps)

modes.label: Sandbox shapes, per-second at list rates (paid from plan credits / top-ups)
modes.note: Size hour = vcpu x $0.03616363 + GiB x $0.01159025 (docs: $0.0000100455/vCPU-s, $0.0000032195/GB-s), billed per second on the allocated shape while running. Storage $0.0001584/GB-h (~$0.1156/GB-month) is on top (storage block). PAUSED sandboxes stop vCPU billing but KEEP billing RAM at $0.01159025/GiB-h plus storage (a paused 4/8 = $0.0927/h = ~$67.7/month). Largest shape per plan: Free 1/1, Beginner 4/4, Pro 8/8, Enterprise 8/16. Shape ids for sub-1-vCPU/odd shapes follow the SDK naming pattern but only s-1vcpu-256mb, s-1vcpu-1gb, s-4vcpu-4gb are confirmed ids. Default disk is 10 GB per sandbox (pricing-page calculator and examples: 10 GB x 720 h x $0.0001584 = $1.14), up to 60 GB; disk bills for the full month whether the sandbox runs or is paused.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: 500 one-time credits (~$5 if 1 credit = $0.01). 1 concurrent, 10 sandboxes/day, 10 GiB max disk, no disks/templates. Top-ups allowed (docs table: 1.2x multiplier).

plans.name: Beginner
plans.note: Slider $10-$50/month = 1,000-5,000 credits/month (fee converted to credits at 100 credits/$). Top-ups get 1.2x credits. 5 concurrent, 50 sandboxes/day, 30 GiB max disk. Largest shape 4 vCPU / 4 GB, so a 4/8 workload needs Pro.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: Slider $75-$200/month = 7,500-20,000 credits/month. Top-ups get 1.5x credits. 20 concurrent, 200 sandboxes/day, 50 GiB max disk, largest shape 8 vCPU / 8 GB.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Docs pricing table: '$200+' per month, 20,000+ credits, 5x top-up multiplier; pricing page: 'Custom' / Contact Sales. 30 concurrent, 300 sandboxes/day, 60 GiB max disk, largest shape 8 vCPU / 16 GB. Self-hosted option for enterprise only.

perf_source: benchmarks.json providers.createos.computesdk: cold_start_tti median 74.65 ms (2026-08-07), burst_tti median 124.89 ms at 100 concurrency (2026-09-25), dax 50.3 s (2026-09-25, 8 vCPU / 15.64 GiB x86_64 = the s-8vcpu-16gb shape). The stale 'createos-sandbox' entry (single July 2026 run: cold start 999.51 ms, burst 1,304.53 ms) measures the same Sandbox product under an older name and is not used. No hpc CPU run.

knobs.label: Credit top-up bonus applied to usage beyond plan credits
knobs.why: Usage is paid in credits; top-ups on Free/Beginner/Pro/Enterprise grant 1.2x/1.5x/1.5x/5x credits per dollar, so usage funded by top-ups costs list/1.2, list/1.5 or list/5. The plan's own monthly credits are at list (100 credits/$).

caveats: USD value of a credit is not stated on the Sandbox pages; 1 credit = $0.01 is from the NodeOps Skills credits page and matches plan math ($10 = 1,000 credits, $75 = 7,500).
Top-up multipliers (1.2x/1.5x/5x) are read as bonus credits per dollar. The 5x Enterprise multiplier implies an 80% effective discount on top-up-funded usage; unverified.

Paused sandboxes keep billing RAM ($0.01159025/GiB-h) plus storage (product page + Limits doc). The SDK docs contradict this ('Compute billing stopped ... only storage costs apply'); the official Limits/product pages are used. Engine paused_ram_billed=true.

Storage $0.0001584/GB-h (~$0.1156/GB-month): which GB are metered (allocated overlay disk vs used, memory snapshot) is not stated; default disk per shape (default_disk_mib) not published. snapshot_gib_month set to the storage rate for the disk part only.
Egress is unmetered ($0) but each sandbox has a 50 GiB default bandwidth quota; the price of rechargeBandwidth top-ups is not published.
Hard caps: concurrency 1/5/20/30 and creation caps 10/50/200/300 sandboxes per day (Free/Beginner/Pro/Enterprise). A 50-concurrent workload exceeds every published plan.
Per-plan CPU/RAM caps on the pricing page (48 / 1,000 / 2,000 cores) are Deploy-platform caps; Sandbox caps come from the Limits doc.
Billing granularity 1 s ('billed per second'); no minimum or creation fee published.

Verify 2026-09-28: createos.sh/pricing/sandbox now says "No tiers, no plan gate, no minimums ... no annual lock-in", while the Limits doc, the Pricing doc table and the product-page FAQ still publish plan tiers with concurrency caps 1/5/20/30. The card keeps the documented tier caps (conservative); if tiers are truly retired, only the rates apply and 50-concurrent workloads may be allowed.

Removed Beginner/Pro annual plans ($8/$60): the only source for "20% off annual" is createos.nodeops.network/pricing, which is the Deploy platform (Plus $49 / Pro $149 plans); the Sandbox pricing page says no annual lock-in and publishes no annual plan.

The rendered createos.nodeops.network/pricing (the CreateOS app's own subscription page, whose sidebar includes Sandbox) DOES show CPU $0.00000095/vCPU-s, Memory $0.00000036/GB-s, Storage $0.00000005/GB-s and plans Free $0 / Beginner $10 / Pro $75 / Enterprise Custom with a Monthly/Annual '20% off' toggle and an 'AI Sandbox' row. The rate cards are not labelled per product; Sandbox pages all use $0.03616363/vCPU-h. The static (non-JS) HTML only contains the Deploy SEO block (Plus $49 / Pro $149), which is probably what the 2026-09-28 check read.

Bandwidth: pricing page says egress is 'Unmetered, any volume $0.00', but each sandbox has a 50 GiB default quota; when exhausted 'Networking pauses ... until it's recharged', and 'Recharge consumes account credit' (price per GiB unpublished; max 100 GiB per recharge call). Egress-heavy sandboxes (>50 GiB each) cost an unknown extra and stop networking by default.
Disk sizes are a fixed menu 10/20/30/40/50/60 GiB (grow online, never shrink), capped by plan max disk 10/30/50/60 GiB.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Set a timeout from 1 minute to 24 hours and the sandbox pauses itself once both API calls and network traffic go quiet.
snapshot_auto.note: Opt-in idle auto-pause (auto_pause_after_seconds 60-86,400; off by default per Limits doc). The idle pause is identical to a manual pause, which is a full Firecracker snapshot: disk + RAM + CPU/device state, so running processes are included (SDK Lifecycle guide: 'When the idle timeout fires, the control plane pauses the sandbox exactly as if you had called pause()'). Restore: 'Wake on request' - hitting a paused sandbox's HTTPS ingress URL resumes it automatically; otherwise resume via API/SDK/CLI. Also self-pause from inside via POST 127.0.0.1:1029. No max session length, so no time-limit trigger. Paused sandboxes still bill RAM + storage.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Pausing snapshots the full VM state to object storage: Disk: filesystem contents Memory: full RAM image (processes, open files, network connections) CPU state: exact register values and execution context
snapshot_on_demand.note: On-demand snapshot = pause (REST POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/pause, SDK pause(), CLI `createos sandbox pause`); memory included. The live VM is torn down while paused (no snapshot-while-running). New machines boot from it via fork: 'Clone a paused sandbox into a new, independent sandbox identity' (own id/IP/placement; any number of forks; S3 disk attachments do not carry over). No named/persistent snapshot objects or snapshot-to-template: templates are Dockerfile builds only, and the AgentBox integration page says 'CreateOS has no matching snapshot feature yet' for checkpoints. Resume keeps the same sandbox id.

harness_api.quote: One pane maps to one sandbox. Your keystrokes go into the microVM; the agent's output comes back.
harness_api.note: No first-party API to start/prompt/stream/resume an agent harness inside the sandbox. Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode / Pi plugins run the agent LOCALLY and use the sandbox as a tool (via the createos CLI). Herdr and Orca integrations (first-party plugins in NodeOps-app/createos-claude-plugins) install and run Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode/Pi/Cursor INSIDE a sandbox, but only as an interactive PTY terminal attached to a Herdr pane / Orca workspace - no prompt/event/conversation API. The Claude Managed Agents guide shows running Anthropic's `ant beta:worker poll` inside a sandbox, but the session API is Anthropic's, not CreateOS's. CreateOS Studio has a runtime 'Sandbox SDK' (start a turn, stream the answer) but that is the separate Studio agent-builder product, not agents in a CreateOS Sandbox microVM. Generic managed-process/PTY APIs exist (exec does not count). Borderline: flip to true only if a PTY-attached Herdr/Orca plugin counts.

egress_allowlist.quote: A non-empty rule list means deny-by-default: only the listed destinations pass; everything else is dropped in-kernel on the host, outside the VM, so code inside the sandbox cannot rewrite or route around the policy.
egress_allowlist.note: Per-sandbox allowlist set at create or live (PUT /v1/sandboxes/{id}/egress, SDK setEgress, CLI `sandbox firewall`); formats host, host:port (80/443 only), *.host, ip, ip:port, cidr, cidr:port. Enforced host-side via eBPF. Domain rules match TLS SNI (HTTPS) or Host header (HTTP), so weak for cleartext HTTP; hostname rules only cover TCP 80/443 (use IP/CIDR for other ports). Default is OPEN (empty list). No denylist token. Private networks between sandboxes are not governed by egress rules.

egress_http_rules.quote: There is no denylist token. To block one destination you must list all destinations you do want.
egress_http_rules.note: Rule grammar is host/IP/CIDR plus port only (full table on the Egress page); matching is on SNI/Host header with no method, path or header rules. The egress-governance page explicitly says enforcement is in-kernel eBPF, not a proxy ('Is this just a proxy I can configure? No.'), so there is no HTTP-level layer.

ingress_rules.quote: Closed. Nothing reaches a sandbox unless ingress_enabled: true, which exposes one HTTPS URL per sandbox.
ingress_rules.note: Control is coarse: a per-sandbox on/off toggle (create-time or live via PATCH / setIngress). When on, any port is reachable at <ulid>-<port>.<domain> with no auth, no per-port choice and no IP allowlist (Claude Code plugin page: 'the URL is the only thing protecting it, there is no authentication in front of it'). Private access paths are authenticated: API-key port tunnels (`createos sandbox tunnel`), SSH gateway with attached public keys, WireGuard VPN into private networks; scoped per-sandbox access tokens for delegating control. No public IPv4.

guest_firewall.quote: Every sandbox is a Firecracker microVM with its own guest kernel, filesystem and network identity.
guest_firewall.note: Not documented explicitly. Firecracker microVM with its own kernel and root access; the devbox:1 image ships Docker 29 (which itself needs iptables/netfilter in the guest). Guest rules sit behind the host-side eBPF egress policy.

secret_proxy.quote: Anything you put into a sandbox is readable by code running in it: envs, files you upload, and the keys of any attached disk, which the sandbox needs to mount the bucket.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are only env vars (envs: write-only through the API, declared at create, 64 keys) or files; disk (S3) credentials are also visible inside the VM. No credential-injecting proxy: egress is eBPF filtering, and the egress-governance page says it is not a proxy. The recommended pattern is to keep credentials on the caller side (e.g. Claude Managed Agents 'sandbox as a tool' topology, or putting only a scoped Anthropic environment key inside). Non-HTTP: n/a.

volume_attach.quote: An S3-compatible bucket registered as a mountable volume. A disk holds its bucket and endpoint configuration; credentials are encrypted at rest and never returned by the API. Disks can be attached to a running sandbox and detached live, and the mount appears inside the guest within about a second.
volume_attach.note: CreateOS 'Disks' are first-party mounts of CUSTOMER-OWNED S3-compatible buckets (AWS S3, R2, MinIO, Tigris), attached at create or live, detachable, optional sub_path - not provider-hosted block/network volumes (no CreateOS storage product billed for them). Root disk is the only provider storage (10 GiB default, raisable via disk_mib to plan max 10/30/50/60 GiB). Answered false for consistency with other bucket-mount-only providers (e.g. langsmith-sandbox); flip to true if customer-bucket mounts count as volumes. Free plan: 0 disks.

volume_shared.quote: Disks are the one thing sandboxes can share. A disk belongs to one account; only that account's sandboxes can attach it. Several of your sandboxes can mount the same disk at once and see the same bucket, with S3's last-write-wins semantics.
volume_shared.note: Read-write (no read-only mount option documented); object storage semantics (last-write-wins), not a POSIX shared filesystem. Same disk can also be mounted at multiple paths in one sandbox. Disk mounts do not carry over to forks.
